name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
summary: A two-arm rowing movement from a hip-hinged position that builds the mid-back and lats and teaches a strong flat-back hinge.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips with soft knees until your torso is about 45 degrees to the floor, back flat.
Let the dumbbells hang below your shoulders with palms facing each other or facing you.
Look at a spot on the floor a little in front of you to keep the neck neutral.
execution: Pull your shoulder blades back and then drive your elbows toward your hips.
Bring the dumbbells to the sides of your lower ribs.
Squeeze your back for a moment at the top.
Lower with control until your arms are straight, without changing your torso angle.
cues: Do not stand up with each rep
mistakes: Rounding the back: lift the chest a little, push the hips back and use lighter weights.
Jerking the weight with body swing: hold your torso still and slow the lowering.
Pulling with the biceps only: think about driving the elbows back.
Rising up as you row: keep the same hinge angle throughout the set.
